newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault commissions study on Vilvoorde options.
newsitem.headline: Renault commissions study on Vilvoorde options.

text.p: French carmaker Renault said on Tuesday that its board had decided to commission an independent study to explore alternatives to the proposed closure of its Vilvoorde assembly plan in Belgium.

"This independent study will allow an economic evaluation of possible measures, within the framework of existing law, to compensate for the cost excesses related to Renault's production stucture," the company said in a statement issued at the start of its annual general meeting.

"In the event that the study leads the company to confirm its initial decision, a plan would be immediately implemented, including on the one hand the appropriate social measures and, on the other hand, the establishment of a significant industrial activity on the site," the statement said.

It said chairman Louis Schweitzer had proposed that another board meeting be held before the end of June at which the directors would examine the results of the study to be conducted by Danielle Kaisergruber of Bernard Bruhnes consultancy.

The statement said that the board had renewed its confidence in Schweitzer and that Tuesday's move was needed given the importance of the proposed plant closure to Renault's economic performance and the social consequences.
